qualityIssues.issue: auth.setup.ts exists but is NOT registered as a setup project. The `projects` array has chromium / dashboard-e2e / onboarding-e2e but none has `dependencies: ['setup']` and there is no `name: 'setup'` project with `testMatch: /auth\.setup\.ts/`. Result: storage state at e2e/.auth/user.json is never created, and ALL existing batch + branch-onboarding specs do their own UI login via a per-test login() helper — slow and brittle.

No project uses `storageState`. Even if auth.setup.ts ran, no spec would consume the cookie. EXECUTE must add a setup project AND add `use: { storageState: 'e2e/.auth/tenant-admin.json' }` to dashboard-e2e and any new journey project.

fullyParallel: false + workers: 1 — every spec runs serially. With 20 new journeys this will become very slow. Consider enabling parallelism per project (the existing batch suites are read-only smoke and parallel-safe).

Test 'dashboard loads after auth' does NOT actually authenticate — it just navigates to /dashboard. Because no project loads storageState, this test is effectively asserting that a redirect to /login happens (URL still contains 'dashboard' as substring of nothing). Misleading test name; either delete or wire to real auth.
Uses page.waitForTimeout(2000) and waitForTimeout(1500). Replace with web-first assertions (expect(locator).toBeVisible()) once data-testids are added.
Uses page.waitForTimeout(1000). Same fix as above.

Captures invite URL via brittle text/regex extraction across multiple fallback strategies. Will be obsolete once data-testid='invite-url-input' is added — EXECUTE should refactor this spec to use the testid (do NOT rewrite, just simplify the helper).
Each describe block calls login() in beforeEach — full UI login per test, 5 files * many tests = enormous wall-clock time. Recommend converting to use storageState once setup project exists.

agentNotes.forExecuteAgent: Critical sequencing: (1) Fix playwright.config.ts FIRST — add a 'setup' project that runs auth.setup.ts and persists storage state to e2e/.auth/tenant-admin.json (rename from user.json), then add `dependencies: ['setup']` and `use: { storageState }` to dashboard-e2e + a new 'journeys-e2e' project. (2) Verify the setup actually produces a usable cookie by running a single test against the new project before adding any data-testids. (3) Then proceed with selector additions in component-file batches — each commit can land independent testids per file without breaking anything. (4) Build seed helpers in parallel with no-seed specs. The 10 'achievable without seeding' journeys (per plan's seedingRequiredVsNot.achievableWithoutSeedHelpers list) should be written FIRST and gated only on testid additions.
blockers: playwright.config.ts auth wiring is broken — must be fixed before any new spec relies on storageState. Without this, EXECUTE will repeat the pattern of UI-login-per-test which is the slowest possible approach.
Zero data-testid attributes exist in production components for any planned selector — all 65 must be added before specs can run. Group additions by component file to minimise PRs.
No user-deletion oRPC endpoint exists; branch-onboarding-full-submit cannot do clean teardown without a new bun script (apps/server/scripts/e2e-cleanup.ts).
Test tenant has no trainer member — commission-rule-cancel/complete journeys need either a direct DB role tweak on admin or a dedicated seeded trainer. Decide BEFORE writing the spec.

Receipt-fallback journey (sales-cancellation-receipt-fallback) is not deterministically reproducible without a direct DB mutation that nulls receipt fields. Plan already flagged this as a P2-deferral candidate — recommend EXECUTE skips it.
Installment-plan journey requires Settings to have at least one configured plan; ensureInstallmentPlanExists() must run as a precondition or test will fail at payment step.
